visual_review.scope: Eight manually inspected images: refresh fixture and installed release memory tab on Debian 12, Ubuntu 24.04, Rocky Linux 8 and Rocky Linux 10
observations: All 14 new rows, complete 64-bit raw register strings, offsets and bit ranges are visible in the scrolled fixture viewport
Synthetic tREFIx9 reads 66 in 1024 DCLK; refresh block wait reads 6 MC DCLK; flags and watermark counts retain distinct units
DDR5 tZQCAL reads 1110 in 2*tCK and tZQLAT reads 293 tCK; DDR4-only tZQCS and tCKESR are marked Not used
tXSDLL and Self_refresh_tCSL display Encoded, and the bottom explanation wraps fully without clipping
Installed release memory tabs start with empty tables, disabled Copy/Save buttons, and no controller registers read
Rocky Linux 10 font metrics retain all new rows, full long field names and the wrapped footer without clipping

limits: Live reads require CPUID Intel family 6 model B7 without a hypervisor, PCI 8086:A700 class 060000 and an already enabled MCHBAR
DDR4/DDR5 aliases and units are field-specific; TXSDLL and TSR remain encoded because the manual does not establish units
Two matching snapshots detect changes but are not atomic hardware measurements; all fixture values are synthetic
Raw refresh configuration includes zero and codes outside recommendations; no training validation, writes, trigger or LPDDR TXSR interpretation is implemented
Other AMD, Intel and board-specific protocols, target hardware and Secure Boot validation remain pending
Portable core validation on Windows/macOS is not a full hardware port

source_research.manual: Intel 743846-001 Rev 001, October 2022; desktop Raptor Lake-S
source_research.findings: TREFIX9 counts 1024 DCLK; RAISE_BLK_WAIT is MC DCLK; ZQCS and TSR have DDR4/DDR5 aliases; TXSDLL and TSR units are not specified; LPDDR TXSR is not decoded
